breakouts.title: Year filter and filtered list

clarified_description: The changelog page currently lists every entry in one long scroll. A reader looking for when something shipped has no way to narrow the view. This change adds a year filter above the entry list: a native `<select>` control with a visible 'Year:' label and an 'All years' default option. The option list is derived from the entries themselves, newest year first, so it never offers a year with no entries and picks up new years automatically as they are added. Selecting a year filters the list in place — no navigation, no URL change, purely client-side component state. The entry count beneath the heading reflects what is currently visible: 'All years' shows the total, and a selected year shows the count for that year.

constraints.detail: `app/changelog/page.tsx` is a server component; any `useState`-based interactivity must live in a `'use client'` child. The filter and its state cannot be added to the page file itself.
`ChangelogList` receives entries pre-sorted newest-first; the filtering step must preserve that order.
Filter selection updates state locally in a single client component and re-renders only the filtered list; no network request, no navigation, no revalidation.

Next.js 16.2.6 is beyond training-data cutoff; `AGENTS.md` directs implementors to read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing code. Client-component directive rules may differ from earlier Next.js versions.

deferred_decisions: Whether YearFilter and ChangelogFilteredList are two files or one is left to the engineer; two is proposed because it keeps the filter testable in isolation, but a single file is acceptable if the engineer prefers it.
The exact Tailwind classes for the <select> and its <label> are left to the engineer, provided they match the surrounding zinc palette and dark-mode treatment already used on the page.

must: The system shall render a year filter control above the changelog entry list and below the entry count line.
The system shall render the year filter as a native HTML `<select>` element.
The system shall label the year filter with a visible 'Year:' label and an `aria-label` of 'Filter entries by year'.
The system shall include an 'All years' option in the year filter and select it by default on initial render.
The system shall derive the list of year options from the dates of the entries in `data/changelog.json` at render time, with no hardcoded years.
The system shall order the year options newest year first, immediately after the 'All years' option.
The system shall list each year at most once in the filter, even when multiple entries share that year.
WHEN the user selects 'All years' the system shall display every entry in the changelog.
WHEN the user selects a specific year the system shall display only entries whose date falls in that year.
WHEN the user changes the selected year the system shall update the visible entry list in place without navigating or changing the URL.
The system shall update the entry count line to reflect the number of entries currently visible after any filter change, using the existing singular/plural wording ('1 entry' / 'N entries').
The system shall preserve the newest-first ordering of entries within any filtered view.
The system shall keep the year filter fully operable by keyboard, using native `<select>` semantics.
The system shall expose the year filter to assistive technologies with an accessible name of 'Filter entries by year'.
outcome: Readers can narrow the changelog to a single year using a keyboard-accessible dropdown above the entry list, and the entry count reflects what they are seeing.
rationale:
The changelog page is a server component today, and both filtering and the count-that-tracks-visible-entries are client concerns. The natural seam is a new `'use client'` wrapper (`ChangelogFilteredList`) that owns the `selectedYear` state, derives the year list from its input entries, filters before passing to the existing `ChangelogList`, and renders both the filter and the count. Moving the count into that wrapper is required by the decision that it reflects the visible set — the server page cannot compute that.

A native `<select>` was chosen over a button group because it is keyboard- and screen-reader-accessible without custom ARIA wiring, matches 'one year at a time', and is the lowest-risk shape given no existing precedent in this codebase for a segmented control. `CopyButton` and `ThemeToggle` are the precedents for a small `useState`-based client component and set the pattern.

Deriving years from the data (rather than hardcoding) is called out both as a requirement and as its own acceptance criterion because it is the behaviour that guarantees the filter stays correct as the changelog grows — this is the discriminating property worth a dedicated test (DTI-01).

The empty and single-year cases are named explicitly (AC7, AC10) because '1 entry' vs 'N entries' and the zero-entry edge are the boundaries that get shipped wrong. The date-format criterion (AC12) applies DTS-04 to the existing entry render path, which is unchanged by this feature but re-covered because the filtered view still shows those dates.

swe_constraints: The new components must begin with `'use client'` on line 1, matching the CopyButton and Tooltip precedents.
Year extraction must come from the entry `date` string, not from a hardcoded array.
The filter's option order is 'All years' first, then years in descending numeric order.
Preserve the newest-first order of entries inside any filtered view — do not re-sort in the wrapper.

Match the existing muted-text styling of the entry count paragraph when the count moves into ChangelogFilteredList (Tailwind zinc palette with dark: prefix, as already used in app/changelog/page.tsx).
The visible 'Year:' label is a `<label htmlFor>` associated with the `<select id>`; the `aria-label` 'Filter entries by year' is on the `<select>` itself.
No URL state: do not read or write `useSearchParams`, `useRouter.push`, or any history API for the selected year.
Props are typed with a local TypeScript interface defined in the same file, matching repo convention.
Do not alter `data/changelog.json`, `ChangelogEntry.tsx`, or the `ChangelogEntryData` type.
Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing client/server boundary code — Next.js 16.2.6 conventions differ from earlier versions.

touches.reason: New client component that owns the selected-year state, derives the year list, filters entries, and renders the filter, the count and the existing ChangelogList.
New presentational client component for the labelled <select>; separated so it can be tested in isolation and reused. Placement in components/changelog/ matches the co-location convention.
Replace the direct render of <ChangelogList> and the total-only entry count paragraph with <ChangelogFilteredList entries={entries} />, so the count and list are driven by the same client state.
New tests covering year derivation, default state, filtering behaviour, count updates, empty state, and keyboard interaction. Mirrors the existing __tests__/changelog/ pattern.
New tests covering the filter's label, accessible name, option order and change events in isolation from the list.

The page no longer renders the entry count paragraph directly; existing assertions on the count's presence and Tailwind classes under the <h1> must be updated (or moved to the ChangelogFilteredList tests).
